relevance_note: The paper reports two siblings with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency, confirmed by "a homozygous mutation in the ALDH5A1 gene (c.1226G>A; p.Gly409Asp)" in the living proband and in the decedent, with both parents heterozygous carriers.
method_note: Read the full Markdown paper (no data tables in it; only Figures 1 and 2, which I did not quote from as tables). No script was used and no table was transcribed, so the v6 (D-31) stacked-cell rule did not apply. Labels: the paper gives no person a label; 'the proband', 'the index patient', 'the decedent', 'the affected sibling' and 'the older sibling' are role words, so rule 6 gives 'unnamed person 1' for the living proband and rule 2 gives 'sister of unnamed person 1' for the decedent; the two parents are named only as 'Both parents', so they are 'parent of unnamed person 1' and 'parent of unnamed person 1 2'. The parents are in scope as relatives who were tested and carry the same variant, so each got a variant row. Contradictions found in the paper: (1) the interval between the decedent's death and her sister's presentation is 'died 6 years earlier' in the Case Report but 'Eight years later, her sister with a neurodevelopmental disorder presented at 13 years of age' in the Abstract, so I recorded no age-at-onset and no age-at-diagnosis for either sibling; (2) the autopsy text says 'there were no gross neuropathologic findings, except for leptomeningeal congestion' and then reports 'Striking bilateral, sharply circumscribed, dark tan discoloration in the deep portion of both globus pallidi'; (3) it says 'No other changes were evident in the other deep cerebral nuclei, including the caudate, putamen, thalamus, and hypothalamus' while Figure 2(D) reports 'Granular perivascular calcification in putamen'. For the checklist item 'T2 hyperintensity of globus pallidus, subthalamic or dentate nuclei on MRI' I recorded the decedent as not reported because her pallidal findings are neuropathologic (discoloration, calcification) and no MRI is reported for her, not as excluded, since the autopsy 'no gross neuropathologic findings' statement is contradicted by the same paragraph. The proband's 'absence of tremor or dyskinesias' was recorded as a phenotypic feature (excluded) but not used to exclude the checklist items dystonia, exertional dyskinesia or hemiballismus. 'The other histologic findings were congestion of small blood vessels in the leptomeninges, globus pallidi, and superior colliculus' was not recorded as a feature because it is a group statement about the decedent's own histology yet is contradicted by the simultaneous statement that there were no gross findings apart from leptomeningeal congestion.
